articles.title: VisionQuest Post-Credits Scene Just Confirmed A Major Marvel Character Is Coming Back in Upcoming Avengers Films
articles.summary: The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.
articles.body:
Spoilers for VisionQuest and potentially Avengers: Doomsday are contained in the article below. You've been warned!

The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.

Following the conclusion of VisionQuest, Marvel snuck in a little teaser for Avengers: Doomsday and/or Secret Wars during the credits. The scene was excluded from advanced screeners provided to the press, so it came as a big surprise and shows that Marvel made a great deal of effort to keep this moment a secret.

The show cut back to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, where Wanda Maximoff, AKA Scarlet Witch, uses her powers to destroy the Darkhold and, in the process, sacrifices herself. Her fate has remained unknown for over four years now, but now, we finally know what's next for her.

Doctor Doom shows up and lifts a bunch of rubble off of her, uttering the words: "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Her eyes open in shock before the scene cuts to black. The plot of Avengers: Doomsday has remained relatively abstract for some time now. Universes are starting to catastrophically collide as part of a series of "incursions," but the why and how of it all has remained a secret. Doom's larger plan and motive have also been kept under wraps, but we've started to get a better idea over the last couple of months.

The post credit scene from the finale of VisionQuest! Well, Wanda’s back! — Spader Lover (Cosmic Muffin Lover) (@SpaderLoverGirl) November 11, 2026

The post credit scene from the finale of VisionQuest! Well, Wanda’s back!

At the end of the recent Avengers: Endgame re-release, we see Doom abduct the Hulk following the events of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . We also saw him try to make contact with a young Franklin Richards at the end of The Fantastic Four: First Steps, though it's unclear if he succeeded in taking him. We have yet to see the powerful child in any of the promo for Doomsday , so it's not out of the question that he has been recruited into some kind of dark army being built by Doom.

It's unclear what other characters may be in Doom's legion, but it's obvious that he's building up an absurdly dangerous level of power that will give the Avengers a run for their money. Many have been wondering how Marvel would top Thanos... and Doctor Doom creating an evil anti-Avengers roster could certainly be the answer. We don't have too much longer to go before we get more answers, as Avengers: Doomsday finally releases next month.

It won't be the end of this story, though. Avengers: Secret Wars is currently slated to release next December, though filming reportedly hasn't even begun... so a delay to 2028 may not be out of the question . Regardless, you can seemingly expect Scarlett Witch to appear in at least one of these projects, if not both.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Wild Oriole Sword - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Wild Oriole Sword is a one-handed weapon in Phantom Blade 0. It has a base damage of 295 and a base Guard Break of 104. It features a five-hit standard
articles.body:
The Wild Oriole Sword is a one-handed weapon in Phantom Blade 0. It has a base damage of 295 and a base Guard Break of 104. It features a five-hit standard combo and a three-hit Sha-Chi combo.

Oriole Song : Press L1+Triangle to consume Sha-Chi to enter the [Oriole Song] state for 10 seconds. While active, every Sha-Chi attack unleashes an air-rending blade wave as piercing as an Oriole's Song Wild

Oriole Sword Art : Pressing L2 consumes 1 Sha-Chi Essence to unleash the Wild Oriole Sword Art, assailing powerful enemies with an unrelenting flurry of sword strikes. This attack is unblockable.

How to Get The Wild Oriole Sword in Phantom Blade 0

In order to get the Wild Oriole Sword in Phantom Blade 0, you'll need to do two things. First, you'll need to find all five ribbons around the Village of Lu that pertain to Mu Xiaokui. After finding all five, you'll then need to finish the main story in the Village of Lu and fight the final boss, Mu Xiaokui, Young Mistress of the Order. Interacting with all five ribbons presents the secret third phase of the fight, and after defeating her, you'll be able to pick up the Wild Oriole Sword on the docks directly in front of you.

The Wild Oriole Sword can be upgraded to gain new buffs and abilities. Below you'll find a table that shows everything you can unlock.

Soul-Tempering the Wild Oriole Sword transforms it into Tianmiao Wild Oriole.

That's everything you need to know about the Wild Oriole Sword in Phantom Blade 0. For more tips and tricks, be sure to check out our weapons , Phantom Edges , and accessories pages.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Season 3’s First Four Episodes Accelerate Sauron’s War and Reenergize the Prime Video Series
articles.summary: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 prove a welcome return to Middle-earth, allowing the series to get back on track after two seasons of wandering.
articles.body:
Some spoilers for Episodes 1-4 of Season 3 and past seasons of The Rings of Power follow. Episodes 1-4 are available on Prime Video now, with Episodes 5 and 6 debuting on Nov. 18, and Episodes 7 and 8 finishing out the season on Nov. 25.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 is a new beginning for the Prime Video series, kicking the story off five years after where things ended in Season 2 , and streamlining the overall narrative into a more cohesive war story.

Season 3 refocuses The Rings of Power on its simple yet compelling good vs. evil premise, jettisoning some past characters and subplots while ensuring the ones remaining all align with the same goal: you exist to either defeat Sauron or to serve him.

Celebrimbor’s death last season means The Dark Lord (Charlie Vickers) isn’t having an easy time forging the One Ring. (Nice touch having Sauron keep Celebrimbor’s skeleton hanging around so his “ghost” – actor Charles Edwards returns for a cameo – can psychoanalyze him about his self-doubts.) Sauron desperately wants to discover whatever secret element Celebrimbor put into the Elven rings, as the Elves have thus far been able to stave off Sauron’s army at the borders of Lindon and Rivendell while nearly everywhere else in Middle-earth has fallen. To aid him in his quest to capture the Elven rings and discern their magic, Sauron has been busy turning mortal men into Nazgûl, promising them eternal life in exchange for becoming his servants of the ring.

Meanwhile, Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) have been busy battling the Orcs (and humans) that Sauron sends after them. Although she hasn’t encountered him in five years, Galadriel is beginning to feel Sauron’s presence again (Robert Aramayo’s Elrond thinks she’s just being paranoid). Galadriel’s past is briefly but sweetly explored here when she meets her future husband, Celeborn (a stalwart Jamie Campbell Bower , back to being a pretty boy following years of Vecna ugliness), during a flashback to the First Age, where they court each other in a wire-fu duel reminiscent of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon .

This sequence, when contrasted with the hardened warrior Galadriel has become, reveals how much she’s changed over a thousand years and the toll the conflict has taken on her. Morfydd Clark’s nuanced performance adeptly captures Galadriel's evolution from romantic to badass in just a few moments of screen time.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Photos

While the ongoing conflict between Sauron and the Elves is the main focus of Season 3, the first four episodes also catch viewers up with the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm, led by now-King Durin IV (Owain Arthur). While there’s some strained humor with the Dwarves, things get interesting with the arrival of Durin’s older brother, Thrain (the always compelling Eddie Marsan, who, even under a mound of makeup, proves an intriguing screen presence). Thrain has an agenda of his own that, by Episode 304, pits brother against brother for control of the dwarf kingdom. Durin and Disa’s (Sophia Nomvete) marriage is put to the test when a misstep from her past comes up, resulting in one of the strongest and most emotional scenes between the two in the whole series thus far.

In addition to Celeborn and Thrain, Season 3 also introduces another curious new addition to the cast in Marnûkh (Adam Young), the “orc with the arc” who initially seems like a willing soldier of Sauron’s but ends up having a more complicated role to play. Marnûkh’s presence puts Galadriel and Arondir’s feelings about Orcs to the test, ultimately leading to tragedy by the end of Episode 304.

Speaking of which, Season 3 also gives Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin), who has not always proved the most interesting character in this show, an Anakin-style arc. A grown man now, Theo has been enslaved by the Númenoreans the last five years, so when a chance presents itself for him to rebel against them – even if it means possibly becoming a Ringwraith for Sauron – he seizes it. This pays off hints that Theo was meant for the dark side that were first seeded in Season 1 when he found that broken sword hilt bearing the sigil of Sauron. He’s a bad guy now but, as with Anakin Skywalker, perhaps redemption is still possible for Theo in the end.

David Weyman’s Gandalf has more of the qualities we associate with the lovable wizard this season, and by Episode 4 his backstory and connection to Ciarán Hinds’ Dark Wizard is revealed (thanks to a Moses-like chat with The Sacred Fire), setting up a more interesting challenge for Gandalf than simply having to battle a fellow sorcerer. I’ll be interested to see how that plays out in the remaining quartet of episodes.

I found the Númenor storyline less compelling than the other plot threads explored in Season 3’s first four episodes, but that’s been my least favorite storyline of the series since Season 1. Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) is a political creature and he has always struck me as a player better suited for a historical drama about intrigue at the royal court than in this particular fantasy tale. He’s a Westeros power player dropped into Middle-earth and whenever the story dwells too long in Númenor, I yearn for it to get back to literally any other character’s plot line.

That said, Ema Horvath’s Eärien gets a key episode this season that realigns her with her father Elendil (Lloyd Owen) and brothers Isildur (Maxim Baldry) and Anárion’s (Andrew Richardson) cause. Given how she broke with them at the end of Season 2, how and why Eärien is now working as their spy goes unexplored (for now). Was that always the case and she was on a long-term undercover mission? Or did she finally see the light after being married to Pharazôn? That remains unclear to me.

And while the first four episodes of Season 3 still offer their share of action (sword fights, arrows, etc.), any grand-scale battles are apparently being held for later in the season once Sauron’s quest to forge the One Ring inches him closer to victory. With the latest trailer teasing a Balrog battle and Sauron wearing the One Ring , I fully expect the latter half of Season 3 to start ramping up the action to epic levels.

articles.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 Review - IGN
articles.summary: In Season 3’s first four episodes, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power smartly gets back to basics. Although not big on epic fight scenes, the real attraction here is the series recalibrating itself, streamlining its plotlines and reminding us that this is, like the original Peter Jackson film trilogy, a simple but compelling story about good needing to triumph over evil. All the show’s most necessary players are back on the board with renewed vigor in what’s a clear attempt at bringing in new viewers to the Prime Video series, while hopefully not alienating those who have stuck with the show thus far.Episodes 1-4 are available on Prime Video now, with Episodes 5 and 6 debuting on Nov. 18, and Episodes 7 and 8 finishing out the season on Nov. 25.
